security_audit.summary: All 41 static alerts are false positives caused by documentation text, example identifiers, or Markdown backticks. The inventory scanner can expose matched source excerpts in terminal or CI logs because its redaction is limited.

remediation.issue: Matched source excerpts may contain sensitive repository content that the current redaction patterns do not recognize.
remediation.suggestion: Default to file paths and rule identifiers only, and require an explicit flag before printing redacted excerpts.

content.user_title: Plan a Safe Migration to Sent
content.value_statement: CPaaS migrations often fail when provider concepts are copied without translation. This skill maps those differences into a phased Sent v3 cutover plan.
actual_capabilities: Scans source repositories for supported provider SDKs, endpoints, status branches, fallback arrays, templates, and consent logic.
Maps Twilio, Sinch, Infobip, Vonage, and MessageBird/Bird concepts to Sent v3 equivalents.
Explains required rewrites for routing, delivery statuses, webhook verification, consent, templates, and tenancy.
Builds a seven-phase migration sequence with verification gates, comparison metrics, rollback triggers, and decommission steps.
Classifies detected source locations as rewrites, new code, reviews, or informational findings.
limitations: The scanner uses regular expressions and may miss configuration-driven senders, generated code, or no-code automations.
The skill does not provision Sent resources, modify production traffic, or revoke provider credentials automatically.
Provider contracts and header names can change, so current vendor documentation still requires verification.
Webhook receiver implementation and production resilience require related specialist skills or direct engineering work.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Migration Areas
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository for CPaaS dependencies. List the files and migration areas that need attention before moving to Sent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner inventory of an existing application

prompt_templates.title: Map One Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Map our [provider] send calls, statuses, webhooks, templates, consent handling, and tenancy model to Sent v3.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cutover Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased Sent cutover plan for [message classes]. Include sandbox gates, live cohorts, dual-run metrics, rollback triggers, and ownership.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Migration Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this migration plan against the Sent mapping and cutover references. Identify unsafe assumptions, missing controls, and unresolved provider differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readiness review before production traffic

output_examples.input: Review a Twilio service that sends SMS and WhatsApp with ordered fallback.
output: Rewrite the ordered channel list because Sent treats multiple channels as a broadcast.
Use automatic routing and preserve one logical send identifier.
Add deterministic idempotency keys before dual-run.
Verify delivery through status events rather than the accepted response.

output_examples.input: Create rollback gates for a staged Sent cutover.
output: Roll back a message class when delivery falls below its agreed tolerance.
Halt immediately when duplicate production messages appear.
Stop retries when credential lockout occurs.
Keep the incumbent receiver active for in-flight callbacks.

best_practices: Run the inventory scanner against the intended repository root and review every result manually.
Verify provider details against current documentation before changing customer-facing behavior.
Use sandbox validation, a small opt-in cohort, and deterministic idempotency keys before increasing traffic.
anti_patterns: Do not copy an ordered fallback array into Sent's channel array.
Do not treat accepted responses or provider handoff as proof of delivery.
Do not retry consent-filtered messages or clear migrated opt-out evidence.

faq.question: Which providers does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Twilio, Sinch, Infobip, Vonage, and MessageBird/Bird migrations to Sent v3.

faq.question: Does the skill change my repository?
faq.answer: No. The included scanner reads eligible files and reports migration findings without modifying source files.

faq.question: Can it execute the production cutover?
faq.answer: No. It prepares mappings, gates, metrics, and rollback steps. Engineers must approve and perform production changes.

faq.question: Why should ordered channel arrays be rewritten?
faq.answer: Sent treats multiple channels as broadcasts, not fallback order. Directly porting an ordered list can create duplicate messages and costs.

faq.question: Does sandbox mode prove full migration readiness?
faq.answer: No. Sandbox validates authentication and payload shape, but live cohorts are required for routing, delivery, templates, and webhook behavior.

faq.question: How are secrets handled by the scanner?
faq.answer: Environment files are skipped and common credential patterns are redacted. Review terminal and CI output because redaction cannot cover every secret format.
